summary: Nimbus Retail — post-failover streaming truncation and unexpected invoice spike
description: Issue summary: After an automated region failover triggered by a noisy-neighbor GPUS pool remediation in us-west, Nimbus Retail observed truncated streaming completions and a simultaneous unexpected billable token spike for multiple routes. Impact: several retail checkout flows received partial responses or abrupt stream termination; billing dashboard shows a 3x token consumption increase for Nimbus' primary API key during the window. Environment: production (us-west) routing through streaming-proxy v2.7.2 and serving-runtime build 5.12.2.
impact: Customer-facing timeouts and truncated streaming responses affecting checkout and price-lookup endpoints. Approximately 62% of streaming sessions for the customer were truncated mid-stream between 2026-03-10T02:14Z and 2026-03-10T03:03Z. Billing shows an anomalous increase in billable tokens tied to repeated re-requests and resumed sessions, resulting in an estimated invoice delta of +$18k for the affected window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Nimbus Retail API key in us-west region with streaming=true and max_tokens=1024. 2) Simulate concurrent checkout flows (10k RPS ramp to 25 RPS concurrently for test tenant). 3) Trigger upstream failover simulation: disable primary GPU pool nodes (simulated via admin toggle) and force traffic to fallback pool. 4) Observe streaming client receives partial events with final 'stream_end' missing; clients re-try and create duplicate token accounting. Note: reproduction requires multi-connection prefix cache warmup to replicate KV cache mismatch behavior seen in production.

investigation_notes: Hypotheses tested: 1) KV prefix-cache deserialization mismatch after pool migration caused serving-runtime to truncate outgoing streams; 2) Streaming-proxy's connection handoff sometimes dropped final chunk+EOS during hot-pool to cold-pool switch; 3) Clients aggressively retrying due to missing EOS resulted in duplicate token accounting in billing pipeline. Findings: 1) Reproduced mismatch by bringing worker containers with different runtime kernel flags into the same pool; prefix length metadata was not normalized across kernel variants. 2) Streaming-proxy handshake had a race where the proxy would acknowledge upstream ready while downstream socket still flushing; this produced truncated client-side streams. 3) Billing pipeline counted resumed sessions as new sessions in a narrow window because session_id rewrite occurred during proxy handoff. Related PRs and configuration diffs captured in linked GitHub PRs.
actions_taken:
- Immediate: Rolled back prefix-cache invalidation and disabled autoscaler drain for the noisy-neighbor pool in us-west to stabilize sessions.
- Hotfix: Applied a temporary streaming-proxy guard to ensure EOS propagated before connection handoff completed.
- Billing: Issued a manual suppression for duplicate token accounting for Nimbus between 2026-03-10T02:12Z and 2026-03-10T03:03Z to prevent customer billing impact while we investigate.
- Eng escalation: Assigned runtime team to produce canonical prefix metadata normalization patch and proxy team to harden handshake race conditions.
resolution_summary: Incident mitigated by rolling back the cache invalidation during pool transition and adding a proxy-level EOS confirmation. Streaming resumed to baseline and the customer was provided with a billing suppression for the anomalous window. Root cause: a combination of prefix-cache metadata mismatch across kernel variants + a proxy handoff race that caused missing EOS leading to client retries and duplicate billing. Permanent fixes are in progress.
follow_up_actions:
1) Runtime team to release v5.12.3 with prefix-metadata normalization (owner: Li Wei) — target 2026-03-17.
2) Proxy team to land handshake guard and add end-to-end session-id propagation tests (owner: Arjun Patel) — target 2026-03-15.
3) Billing to implement idempotent session accounting and de-dup logic for replays during handoffs (owner: Priya Rao) — target 2026-03-24.
4) Post-incident review with Nimbus Retail and Customer Success (scheduled 2026-03-13) to review root cause and credit invoice as appropriate.
5) Run a full simulated failover exercise in staging with KV cache normalization enabled before next public rollout.
